note: Uremic rats predicted PTH suppression, on-target hypocalcemia and the GI-sparing of the newer calcimimetics correctly; their parathyroid-hyperplasia and vascular-calcification predictions have never been tested in patients on a member drug.
label: SHPT (CaSR PAMs)

engagement.note: Etelcalcetide (AMG 416) lowered PTH and serum calcium dose-dependently in normal, 1K1C and 5/6-nephrectomy rats; no patient PD yet published.
engagement.quote: Administration of AMG 416 in vivo into either normal or renally compromised rats results in dose-dependent reductions in parathyroid hormone (PTH) levels and corresponding decreases in serum calcium, regardless of the baseline level of PTH.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; the 5/6 Nx and 1K1C studies are described in full in the FDA pharmacology review (NDA 208325).

engagement.note: Hemodialysis patients: PTH fell 49.4% at 10 mg and 33.0% at 5 mg thrice weekly over 4 weeks, as the rat PD predicted. Ruling (rule 6): dated 2013, when Martin 2014 (NDT, online Nov 2013) showed iPTH falling dose-dependently in healthy volunteers, who count for engagement.
engagement.quote: treatment with AMG 416 at 10 mg (Cohort 2) and 5 mg (Cohort 3) for up to 4 weeks resulted in mean 49.4% and 33.0% reductions from baseline in PTH during the efficacy assessment phase
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading of both papers. The phase 1 single-dose PD paper (Martin 2014, NDT) would date the match a year earlier but was not retrieved.
engagement.reason: Rat PTH fall reproduced in patients
engagement.judgement: My juxtaposition of Walter 2013/2014 (rat) with Bell 2015 (patients); no source states both. Readout is PTH, the parathyroid output the receptor controls, hence proximal; serum calcium is downstream. Magnitude within_2x on fractional PTH reduction: ~50% sustained in 5/6 Nx rats at 1 mg/kg daily (Walter 2014, doi:10.1186/1471-2369-15-81) vs 49.4% at 10 mg in patients. Evocalcet (Kawata 2018 rat -> Akizawa 2018 phase 2b dose-response, doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0204896) and upacicalcet (Goto 2023 rat -> Shigematsu 2023) repeated the match with no status change.
engagement.magnitude_basis: fractional PTH reduction: ~50% in 5/6 Nx rats (1 mg/kg daily IV) vs 49.4% in patients at 10 mg thrice weekly

engagement.model: Patient-derived primary parathyroid cells ex vivo (primary HPT adenoma tissue)
engagement.note: Etelcalcetide lowered PTH secretion in 4 of 8 calcium-responsive cultures from primary-HPT adenomas (EC50 0.42-20.8 uM); no SHPT tissue, no patient comparison.
engagement.short: Human parathyroid cells: PTH falls in 4/8
engagement.quote: In four of the eight parathyroid cell cultures which responded extracellular Ca2+, etelcalcetide reduced hormone secretion with the 50% effective concentrations of 0.57, 20.8, 0.42, and 0.57 µmol/L.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (PMID 33047189; epub 2020-10-12, print 2021). Tissue is primary-HPT adenoma, not SHPT gland; the paper itself says SHPT-derived cells are needed. EC50s (0.42-20.8 uM) sit far above clinical plasma exposure, so a magnitude comparison would likely fail.
engagement.judgement: Untested, not retro: the system was first run in 2020, after patient PTH lowering was known (the paper says so), so any future comparison on this track scores retro, never same; but the paper makes no model-vs-patient comparison (4 of 8 cultures responded; nobody asked whether ex-vivo sensitivity picks responders) and its tissue is a different disease. Class-level because the question asked was whether the drug acts directly on human parathyroid cells; a patient-level use (per-culture sensitivity) has not been made. Readout is PTH secretion, the receptor's own output, hence proximal.

dose.note: Rat PK: linear, half-life 2-4.5 h, PTH suppressed at 0.3-1 mg/kg IV; no human exposure target stated.
dose.short: Rat PK and effective dose only
dose.quote: No drug accumulation was observed under this dosing regimen, and the terminal half-life of AMG 416 was estimated to be 2-4.5 hours.

dose.note: Rule ruling: the general-toxicology margin was below 1 (rat 0.7x, dog 0.15x), so the model predicted the effective dose would not be tolerated; patients were titrated to 15 mg and reached target. FDA calls the margin an over-prediction: contra, model first public after the 2014 patient data.
dose.short: Rat margin <1x; patients dosed to target
dose.quote: Therefore, these safety margins significantly over-predict human risk.
dose.confidence_note: FDA PharmR (NDA 208325) safety-margin section, read in the source bundle. The earlier quote was the fertility NOAEL (1.8x), not the general-toxicology margin. EMA EPAR (2016) also says 'no safety margins' (not re-read here).
dose.judgement: Decision 16 settled: the model stated no exposure target, and its stated tolerability margin (NOAEL below patient exposure) did not hold: patients were dosed to the target exposure with hypocalcemia managed by titration (1% discontinued). The regulator itself says the margins over-predict human risk, so contra, margin_stated true, not blocked_by toxicity. The hypocalcemia itself is scored in safety. Retrodiction true: the margin was first public in the 2016-17 regulator reviews, after the 2014 phase 3 announcements.
dose.magnitude_basis: AUC at the 6-month rat NOAEL (1 mg/kg/day) was 0.7-fold the patient exposure at 15 mg TIW (dog 0.15-fold); patients were dosed to 15 mg and reached the PTH target

dose.note: Evocalcet suppressed PTH in 5/6-nephrectomy rats at lower oral doses than cinacalcet because of higher bioavailability; no human exposure target stated.
dose.short: Rat oral dose range, higher bioavailability
dose.quote: The pharmacological effects of evocalcet were observed at lower doses because of its higher bioavailability than cinacalcet, which may have contributed to the reduced GI tract symptoms.
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; rat dose numbers not extracted.

dose.note: Oral evocalcet titrated 1-12 mg/day brought 72.7% of hemodialysis patients to the PTH target, non-inferior to cinacalcet; the rat dose range translated. Ruling: retrodiction. Evocalcet's own phase 3 result was announced 31 Jan 2017 (72.7% at target, Nov 2017), before the rat dose data were public (PMDA review Mar 2018, Kawata Apr 2018).
dose.short: Oral dose range reached PTH target
dose.quote: In the evocalcet and cinacalcet groups, 72.7% and 76.7%, respectively, achieved the target intact parathyroid hormone level (between-group difference: -4.0% [95% confidence interval -11.4%, 3.5%], for non-inferiority).
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level; no exposure (AUC) comparison between rat and patient is published, so magnitude is null. NCT02549391 has no posted results.
dose.reason: Oral dose range reached PTH target
dose.judgement: Dose is split by modality (two groups on the tile). Evocalcet is the first small-molecule member in patients; my pairing of Kawata 2018 (rat) with Fukagawa 2018 (patients). Upacicalcet repeated it: IV 0.03-3 mg/kg in rats (Goto 2023, doi:10.1016/j.ejphar.2023.175936) and 67% vs 8% at target in patients (Shigematsu 2023), no status change. ASP-7991's phase 2 (NCT02133404, 2014) has no results or publication, so it adds nothing.

dose.model: Population PK/PD model of etelcalcetide (PTH-calcium homeostasis, CaSR cooperativity)
dose.quote: The maximum response Emax and the potency parameter EC50 were estimated to be 0.69 and 21.0 ng/mL, respectively.
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level (PMID 24752908, epub 2014-05-02). Indirect-response iPTH model on single-dose healthy-male data; the patient population model with calcium (Chen 2016) came later.
dose.note: First PK/PD model (healthy males, single IV dose): three-compartment PK, iPTH indirect response, EC50 21 ng/mL; no patient regimen yet tested.

dose.model: Population PK/PD model of etelcalcetide (PTH-calcium homeostasis, CaSR cooperativity)
dose.note: Pre-phase-3 population model picked 5 mg TIW start, week-3 sampling, week-4 titration to 15 mg; that scheme reached the PTH target in 74-75% of phase 3 patients. Ruling: retrodiction. The model's regimen claim was first public (Chen 2016, online Sept 2016) after etelcalcetide's own phase 3 results (Aug 2014); it reproduces them.
dose.quote: Based on the proposed titration scheme, in the pivotal Phase 3 trial the primary efficacy endpoint (proportion of subjects achieving >30% reduction in PTH from the baseline) was 74.0% in Study 20120229 and 75.3% in Study 20120230.
dose.confidence_note: FDA review text (NDA 208325 ClinPharmR, sections 2.3 and 4.2.4); Chen 2016 full text read via Europe PMC (PMC5036423). Chen 2016's model was fit on phase 1 (20130139) and phase 2a/2b only and its simulations set the registration-trial regimen, so the regimen prediction is prospective; the review's final PKPD model also included the two phase 3 trials.
dose.judgement: Separate in-silico track: a different system (semi-mechanistic PK/PD model) making its own prediction (which starting dose, frequency and titration timing will hit the >30% PTH target with acceptable calcium). Chen 2016: 'these results support the selected 5 mg dose as a safe and efficacious starting dose, as well as the TIW dosing frequency in registration trials that target >30% change in PTH'. The regulator states model-based simulations supported the titration scheme used in phase 3 and gives that scheme's result, so comparison_stated true. Reached and worked: same. Not a decision-16 margin (no NOAEL/MTD statement), margin_stated false; hypocalcemia scored on this track's safety cell. Magnitude on the responder fraction is partly a fit (final model included phase 3), hence medium confidence.
dose.magnitude_basis: responder proportion: ~75% simulated to reach >30% PTH reduction after 12 weeks of titration (final PKPD model, Table 16) vs 74.0% and 75.3% observed

efficacy.note: Etelcalcetide in 5/6-nephrectomy rats lowered PTH, attenuated parathyroid hyperplasia and reduced vascular calcification; nothing yet compared in patients.
efficacy.quote: Treatment of 5/6 nephrectomized rats with AMG 416 resulted in dramatic improvements in their metabolic profile, including lower PTH and serum creatinine levels, reduced amounts of vascular calcification, attenuated parathyroid hyperplasia
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level; the FDA pharmacology review describes the same 5/6 Nx studies and an adenine-rat calcification study.

efficacy.note: Primary endpoint (>30% PTH fall, weeks 20-27) met: 74.0% and 75.3% vs 8.3% and 9.6% on placebo in two phase 3 trials. Ruling (rule 6): dated 2014, when Amgen announced (18 Aug 2014) 74.0% vs 8.3% reaching the >30% PTH endpoint; the JAMA paper still sets the status.
efficacy.quote: Patients randomized to etelcalcetide were significantly more likely to achieve the primary efficacy end point: in trial A, 188 of 254 (74.0%) vs 21 of 254 (8.3%; P < .001)
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading of Block 2017; the FDA summary review (NDA 208325) carries the same 74%/8% and 75%/10% table.
efficacy.reason: PTH primary endpoint met as predicted
efficacy.judgement: Four calls. (1) SHPT is defined by PTH, so the PTH primary endpoint is the disease responding; the rat's hyperplasia and vascular-calcification predictions have never been tested on a member drug (no outcomes or calcification trial for etelcalcetide, evocalcet or upacicalcet), so outcome_tested is null; EVOLVE and ADVANCE were cinacalcet, not a member, and are set aside. (2) Dated 2014 on Amgen's phase 3 top-line press release (18 Aug 2014), earlier than Bell 2015's phase 2 and the 2017 paper. (3) My pairing of Walter 2013 with Block 2017; the FDA review describes both but does not put them side by side. (4) Magnitude within_2x on fractional PTH reduction (~50% in rats vs 55%, 849 to 384 pg/mL, in trial A). Evocalcet (Fukagawa 2018) and upacicalcet (Shigematsu 2023; Kendrick 2026) met their PTH primary endpoints too, no status change. ASP-7991 phase 2 (NCT02133404) never reported.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: fractional PTH reduction: ~50% in 5/6 Nx rats vs 55% mean (849 to 384 pg/mL) in trial A

patient_trials.quote: Etelcalcetide was noninferior to cinacalcet on the primary end point.
In the evocalcet and cinacalcet groups, 72.7% and 76.7%, respectively, achieved the target intact parathyroid hormone level
The percentage of participants achieving mean serum iPTH concentrations of 60-240 pg/ml during the evaluation period was 67% (69/103) in the upacicalcet group and 8% (4/50) in the placebo group.
in PATH-1, 42.1% versus 16.8%, for a difference in proportions of 25.3% (95% confidence interval, 16.2 to 34.5, P < 0.001)
in PATH-2, 43.5% versus 17.4%, for a difference in proportions of 26.1% (95% confidence interval, 17.4 to 34.8, P < 0.001)

efficacy.model: Population PK/PD model of etelcalcetide (PTH-calcium homeostasis, CaSR cooperativity)
efficacy.quote: The maximum response Emax and the potency parameter EC50 were estimated to be 0.69 and 21.0 ng/mL, respectively.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level (PMID 24752908, epub 2014-05-02). Indirect-response iPTH model on single-dose healthy-male data; the patient population model with calcium (Chen 2016) came later.
efficacy.note: Healthy-subject iPTH model only; the paper itself says PK/PD studies in hemodialysis patients are still needed, so no efficacy prediction tested.
efficacy.short: iPTH model, patients not yet modelled

efficacy.model: Population PK/PD model of etelcalcetide (PTH-calcium homeostasis, CaSR cooperativity)
efficacy.note: Model predicted the 5 mg-start titration scheme would meet the >30% PTH primary endpoint in ~75% of patients; trials A/B: 74.0% and 75.3% vs 8.3% and 9.6% placebo. Ruling: retrodiction. The model was first public (Chen 2016, FDA 2017) after phase 3 results were announced in 2014, and the final model was fit on those trials; it reproduced them.
efficacy.quote: Approximately 75% of subjects are expected to achieve the primary efficacy endpoint following 12 weeks of titration.
efficacy.confidence_note: The ~75% figure is the applicant's final PKPD simulation (Table 16), from a model whose dataset included phase 3 studies 20120229/20120230, so the number-level agreement is partly a fit. The prospective statement (Chen 2016, pre-phase-3 model) was qualitative: the regimen targets >30% PTH change. A stricter reader scores this cell retro.
efficacy.reason: Fit model reproduced known PTH result
efficacy.judgement: Scored same on the prospective element: the pre-phase-3 model chose the regimen and stated it would reach the >30% PTH target, and the pivotal trials met that primary endpoint on it (Block 2017, doi 10.1001/jama.2016.19456). The ~75% number is a post-hoc refinement and is recorded only as magnitude. Dose and efficacy are one success counted once (dose same, efficacy same). outcome_tested null: no outcome trial on this model's prediction.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: proportion achieving >30% PTH reduction: ~75% simulated vs 74.0% (trial A) and 75.3% (trial B)

safety.note: Rats dosed with etelcalcetide lost serum calcium with PTH, naming on-target hypocalcemia as the liability; dog telemetry later tied QTc prolongation to it.
safety.quote: dose-dependent reductions in parathyroid hormone (PTH) levels and corresponding decreases in serum calcium, regardless of the baseline level of PTH
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level; the dog QTc and 6-month rat hypocalcemia findings are in the FDA pharmacology review, first public 2017.

safety.note: Held: blood calcium decreased 64% vs 10%, symptomatic hypocalcemia 7% vs 0.2%, QTcF rise >60 ms 1.2% vs 0%; rodent GI toxicity matched upper-GI bleeds. Ruling: dated 2014, when Amgen reported blood calcium decreased 61.0% vs 8.3% (symptomatic 7.2% vs 0.4%). The heart-failure warning is not a missed harm: the label ties it to falling calcium, which the rat predicted.
safety.short: Hypocalcemia, QTc and GI harms held
safety.quote: Prolongation of QTc interval is a known consequence of hypocalcemia in the dog and in humans.
safety.confidence_note: Patient rates are from the Parsabiv label (208325Orig1s000Lbledt) and the FDA summary review, which states the rodent GI-mucosa finding beside the three upper-GI-bleed deaths.
safety.judgement: On-target harm, so pooled across modalities. The regulator itself puts dog QTc and human hypocalcemia side by side (comparison_stated true). Hypocalcemia was dose-limiting in the 6-month rat study (NOAEL 1 mg/kg) and the most common patient reaction; the summary review says rodent studies 'appeared to demonstrate a Parsabiv-related toxic effect on the gastro-intestinal mucosa' against three upper-GI-bleed deaths. Not scored: the heart-failure hospitalisation imbalance (2% vs 1%), which no species flagged and FDA attributes to the class with unknown mechanism; too weak to call a missed harm. Evocalcet and upacicalcet repeated the hypocalcemia match (decreased calcium the leading adverse event in Fukagawa 2018, Shigematsu 2023, Kendrick 2026), no status change.
safety.magnitude_basis: hypocalcemia-driven QTc prolongation and serum-calcium fall, dog/rat vs patients; no rate comparable across species

safety.model: Rat gastric emptying and marmoset emesis vs cinacalcet
safety.note: Evocalcet, unlike cinacalcet, did not delay gastric emptying in rats and caused less emesis in marmosets: a prediction of fewer GI adverse events.
safety.short: Rat and marmoset predict GI sparing
safety.quote: With regard to the gastro-intestinal effects, cinacalcet induced a significant delay in gastric emptying in rats, while evocalcet did no marked effects on it.
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level. Published 2018-04-03, after the head-to-head trial ended (2016-11), but the GI-sparing premise is stated in the 2014 phase 2b, so the experiments predate the trial; not a retrodiction. Evocalcet is PMDA-approved; whether this model was in the Japanese filing is unverified (model_filed null).

safety.model: Rat gastric emptying and marmoset emesis vs cinacalcet
safety.note: Head-to-head phase 3: GI-related adverse events 18.6% on evocalcet vs 32.8% on cinacalcet, superiority shown, as the rat and marmoset predicted. Ruling: retrodiction. Kyowa Hakko Kirin announced the lower upper-GI incidence vs cinacalcet on 31 Jan 2017, before the rat/marmoset data were public (Kawata 2018).
safety.quote: The incidence of gastrointestinal-related adverse events was 18.6% and 32.8%, respectively (between-group difference: -14.2% [-20.9%, -7.5%], significant for superiority).
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level; the trial abstract states the GI-sparing rationale but not the animal data, so the comparison is mine. NCT02549391 has no posted results.
safety.judgement: Separate track: a different model (gastric emptying, emesis) making a different prediction (less GI harm than cinacalcet) from the uremic rat. The harm is a class effect (nausea/vomiting with CaSR agonism), so pooled, no modality. Direction only: a gastric-emptying delay and an adverse-event rate are not the same quantity.
safety.magnitude_basis: rat gastric-emptying delay (absent vs ~50% with cinacalcet) against patient GI adverse-event rate (18.6% vs 32.8%)

safety.model: Rat gastric emptying and marmoset emesis vs cinacalcet
safety.note: Second drug: upacicalcet left rat gastric emptying untouched at 300x the effective dose; in patients upper-GI events matched placebo. Ruling: retrodiction. Upacicalcet's own patients were reported first (phase I/II, online June 2022: mild upper-GI symptoms at higher doses), before the rat data (Goto 2023, online Aug 2023).
safety.short: Upacicalcet: GI events equal to placebo
safety.quote: The incidence of upper gastrointestinal adverse events, such as nausea and vomiting, was similar between the two groups.
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level. The rat paper (Goto 2023, epub 2023-08-02) was published after the trial finished (2019-12) and after Japanese approval (2021); when the gastric-emptying experiments were run is unverified, so a stricter reader could call this a retrodiction. Placebo-controlled, so the sparing is relative to placebo, not cinacalcet.
safety.judgement: Strengthens, not a status change. PATH-1/PATH-2 (Kendrick 2026, doi:10.1681/ASN.0000001285, NCT05832931/NCT05836220, no results posted) repeat it: 'Rates of gastrointestinal symptoms were similar between treatment groups.'
safety.magnitude_basis: rat gastric emptying (no effect up to 10 mg/kg) against patient upper-GI adverse-event rate (similar to placebo)

safety.model: Population PK/PD model of etelcalcetide (PTH-calcium homeostasis, CaSR cooperativity)
safety.quote: The maximum response Emax and the potency parameter EC50 were estimated to be 0.69 and 21.0 ng/mL, respectively.
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level (PMID 24752908, epub 2014-05-02). Indirect-response iPTH model on single-dose healthy-male data; the patient population model with calcium (Chen 2016) came later.
safety.note: Healthy-subject model of iPTH only; serum calcium was not modelled, so no hypocalcemia prediction yet.

safety.model: Population PK/PD model of etelcalcetide (PTH-calcium homeostasis, CaSR cooperativity)
safety.note: Model predicted dose-dependent calcium lowering kept acceptable by titration; label: calcium <8.3 mg/dL in 79% vs 19%, <7.5 in 27% vs 5.5%, symptomatic hypocalcemia 7% vs 0.2%, 1% discontinued. Ruling: retrodiction. The calcium prediction was first public (Chen 2016) after etelcalcetide's own patients showed calcium falling (Amgen, Aug 2014).
safety.quote: The results also suggest that the starting dose of 5 mg followed by titration algorithm implemented in phase 3 is expected to provide reasonable Ca lowering, while maintaining an acceptable safety profile, compared to other fixed dosing regimens simulated
safety.confidence_note: Patient rates from the Parsabiv label (208325Orig1s000Lbledt, Description of Selected Adverse Reactions). The simulated '<6% with cCa <7.5 mg/dL' is a per-visit proportion from the final model; the label's 27% is patients with at least one value below 7.5 mg/dL over 26 weeks, so the two numbers are not the same quantity and no magnitude is computed.
safety.reason: Calcium claim public after patient data
safety.judgement: On-target harm, pooled across modalities. Direction held: calcium fell dose-dependently (Chen 2016 prospectively: 'Ca response was predicted to be delayed and less pronounced (<8%)' at 5 mg), hypocalcemia was the leading adverse reaction, yet the titration algorithm the model supported kept discontinuations at 1% and the regulator called the profile acceptable. A stricter reader could set contra on the simulated <6% versus 27% with any value below 7.5 mg/dL; I read those as different quantities. The same harm is also scored on the rat-dog-tox track; each track is scored on its own prediction.
safety.magnitude_basis: corrected serum calcium: simulated dose-dependent fall with <6% per-visit below 7.5 mg/dL under titration vs 27% of patients with at least one value below 7.5 mg/dL

safety.model: Cynomolgus monkey safety pharmacology and 4-39 week toxicology (evocalcet)
safety.note: Monkey telemetry and repeated-dose studies showed QTc prolongation timed to the serum-calcium fall, 0.4-fold margin; in-vitro ion-channel and papillary-muscle studies ruled out direct channel block.
safety.quote: an increase in heart rate, an increase in blood pressure, and QTc prolongation in monkeys (Table 7), with 4.0- and 0.4-fold safety margins in rats and monkeys, respectively.
safety.confidence_note: Full text of the PMDA English review (dated 2018-03-08), section 3.1.3 and Table 7; the monkey data were not public before it, so first use is proxied by the review year.

safety.model: Cynomolgus monkey safety pharmacology and 4-39 week toxicology (evocalcet)
safety.note: Held in direction: QT-prolongation events in 1.6% (8/493) of Japanese phase III patients, 3 judged drug-related, none serious; PMDA attributes the risk to decreased blood calcium, as the monkey did.
safety.quote: Adverse events coded to torsade de pointes/QT prolongation occurred in 1.6% (8 of 493) of patients in all evocalcet groups combined.
safety.confidence_note: Both sides from the same PMDA review (section 3.1.3 monkey, section 7.R QT events, Table 49), paired here rather than stated by PMDA; no ECG-interval rate comparable to the monkey QTc. Registry ids of the Japanese phase III studies not looked up.
safety.reason: Monkey hypocalcemic QTc reproduced as QT events
safety.judgement: A separate system from rat-dog-tox (different species, different member, no shared source). The monkey call was QTc prolongation secondary to hypocalcemia, not channel block; patients showed QT-prolongation events at low rate (0.9% vs 2.8% on cinacalcet) that PMDA ties to decreased blood calcium. Direction matches; partial because the rate was not above the active comparator.
safety.magnitude_basis: hypocalcemia-linked QTc prolongation in monkeys vs QT-prolongation adverse events in patients; no comparable rate

safety.model: Rat gastric emptying and marmoset emesis vs cinacalcet
safety.note: Opening entry of the upacicalcet track: rat gastric emptying (no marmoset arm), first public after the drug's own patient data; the comparison is scored retro in entry 5.
safety.quote: Furthermore, upacicalcet did not affect gastric emptying in normal rats when administered up to a dose of 10mg/kg (300-fold higher than the dose affecting serum iPTH levels), while the administration of cinacalcet significantly slowed gastric emptying by approximately 50%.
